analysis.title: Goldman's Pasquariello On The 'Tug-Of-War' Between Stocks & Bonds
key_insights: Tony Pasquariello (Goldman global head of hedge fund coverage) says the bond market is on thin ice. 2-year notes are up 145 bps YTD and 10-year notes yield the most since summer 2007. Real yields, shown in a 25-year chart of 10-year TIPS, now carry a meaningful risk premium.

Higher real yields hurt zero-yield assets, and Pasquariello says he is taking losses in gold. They also raise the bar for Corporate America to keep up the earnings growth that has offset the macro stress.

The S&P 500 has been range-bound around 7700 for two months and speculative accounts have cut a significant amount of US equity length. The index is still about a weekly straddle from its all-time high and NDX made a higher high as recently as last Tuesday.

Rate-sensitive groups are paying the price below the index surface. Drawdowns from local highs are biotech -8%, small cap -9%, REITs -10%, homebuilders -15%, utilities -15% and non-profitable tech -19%.
Index resilience is attributed to mega cap tech, which keeps getting thesis-affirming news such as Meta's Muse and a large NVDA buyback.
10-year yields have risen for seven consecutive months while inflation breakevens have barely moved. Pasquariello concludes that inflation is not the primary driver of the backup, unlike 2022.

Ben Snider's point: 10-year yields went from 4.14% to 5.27% in a year and the S&P forward P/E fell from 23x to 19x, yet the spread between S&P earnings yield and 10-year yields has stayed steady. Stocks are repricing for rates through a lower multiple and are being carried by earnings growth.

Bear case: when 10-year yields rise 2 standard deviations in a month, the S&P usually shows strain. In today's terms that is about 50 bps, and the rule of thumb was just triggered. The speed limit is most acute when real yields drive the move.

Bull case, from Rich Privorotsky: in 1999 the Fed hiked three times starting in late June and the 10-year went from 5.78% to 6.44% while NDX rallied 61% and later doubled from the October 1999 low to the March 2000 high. Pasquariello warns to be careful with big shorts while the primary equity trend is higher.

Pasquariello views higher rates as a headwind to stocks and not a wrecking ball, absent an inflation surge or a credit problem. He expects healthy earnings growth, in line with Goldman's forecast, and still worries about debt and deficits.

He cites his 2007 notes: credit and mortgage markets were failing before equities broke. Stocks can coexist with a bumpy Treasury market, but it is a different situation when funding and credit markets seize up. US investment grade has held up reasonably well so far.

Execution construct: it is a bull market and the primary trend is higher. Core US equity length should be paired with trading length in commodities (BCOM and GSCI have worked this year) and a trading short in fixed income expressed through options.

Options currently offer inexpensive tail hedges on sectors most sensitive to financial stress. Dom Wilson notes these hedges help most if the asset mix is long stocks, long commodities and short bonds.

sector_views.rationale: Index heavyweights have kept advancing on a steady stream of thesis-affirming news and are the main reason the headline index has held up despite higher yields.

sector_views.sector: Rate-sensitive sectors (biotech, small cap, REITs, homebuilders, utilities, non-profitable tech)
sector_views.rationale: These groups are down 8% to 19% from local highs as yields rise. The note describes them as paying a clear price but gives no explicit rating.

earnings_insights: Earnings growth has been strong enough to counteract the macro stress from higher yields, and Goldman forecasts healthy growth to continue (see Goldman note 'Over-earnings, but not an earnings bubble').
S&P forward P/E fell from 23x a year ago to 19x now while the earnings yield spread to 10-year yields stayed steady, so profit growth has offset the multiple compression.
Mega cap tech news flow cited as supportive: Meta's Muse and a large NVDA buyback (no EPS or revenue figures given).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Front-end repricing is large. It is part of the bond market selloff that Pasquariello says is on thin ice.
Highest since summer 2007, rising seven consecutive months. Real yields are driving it, with breakevens little changed.

macro_indicators.reading: barely changed over the seven-month rise in 10-year yields
macro_indicators.interpretation: Inflation is not the main driver of the yield backup, which separates this episode from 2022.
The historical trigger for S&P strain was just hit, and it is most acute when real yields drive the move.

macro_indicators.reading: 5.78% to 6.44% from first Fed hike to year-end 1999
macro_indicators.interpretation: NDX rallied 61% over that stretch, showing equities can rise through higher yields when the primary trend is up.

trade_ideas.description: Keep core length in US equities, add trading length in commodities (BCOM and GSCI exposure) and a trading short in fixed income expressed through options
trade_ideas.rationale: Primary trend in equities is higher, but rising real yields and a debt and deficit backdrop argue for a commodity and short-bond offset.
trade_ideas.risk: An inflation surge or a credit and funding market seizure would turn higher rates from a headwind into a wrecking ball for stocks.

trade_ideas.description: Buy inexpensive options tail hedges on the sectors most sensitive to financial stress, alongside long stocks, long commodities and short bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: Tail hedges are cheap now and would pay off in a credit-stress scenario against that asset mix.

risk_factors: A 2 standard deviation monthly rise in 10-year yields, driven by real yields, has historically preceded S&P strain and was just triggered.
Credit or funding market stress. Pasquariello compares it to the 2007 sequence from sub-prime into structured product, investment grade, high yield and equities.
An inflation surge, which would change higher rates from a headwind into a wrecking ball.
Liquidity withdrawal by the Fed and the bumpy early innings of a tightening cycle.
Debt and deficit risk, which Pasquariello expects to worry about for a good while.
Real yield pressure on zero-yield assets such as gold.
Earnings growth has to keep up, since higher rates raise the bar for Corporate America.
charts_described: Chart of 10-year TIPS yields going back 25 years, presented by Pasquariello as showing real rates now carry a good dose of risk premium.
vol_and_positioning: Speculative accounts have cut a significant amount of length in US equities after two months of range trading in the S&P around 7700.
The S&P is described as just a weekly straddle away from its all-time high.
Options offer inexpensive tail hedges on the sectors most sensitive to financial stress, and the bulls should take advantage of that.
A trading short in fixed income can be expressed simply through the options market.
geopolitical: The introduction describes traders switching daily between caring about AI, oil or rates, and frames an administration as trying to exhaust traders' risk budgets so they stop buying crude. This is the ZeroHedge editor's framing, not the Goldman note's.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings growth is offsetting higher yields. The S&P multiple fell from 23x to 19x but the spread of earnings yield over 10-year yields stayed steady. Mega cap tech keeps getting supportive news, and 1999 saw NDX up 61% while 10-year yields rose from 5.78% to 6.44%.
tension_points.bear_case: A 2 standard deviation monthly rise in 10-year yields (about 50 bps) has just occurred, historically a sign of S&P strain, especially when real yields drive it. Rate-sensitive groups are already down 8% to 19%, and the bond market is on thin ice.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An inflation surge or a credit problem, such as funding and credit markets seizing up, which would turn higher rates from a headwind into a wrecking ball.

theme_stances.key_argument: Absent an inflation surge or a credit problem, higher rates weigh on stocks but earnings growth keeps the primary trend higher.
theme_stances.evidence: I view higher rates as a headwind to stocks, NOT as a wrecking ball.

theme_stances.key_argument: Pair core equity length with a trading short in fixed income because real yields now carry risk premium and debt and deficit risk persists.
theme_stances.evidence: a trading short in fixed income (expressed simply through the options market)
